sentences.text: Jade Pritchard is the mother of Lily and Mason.
Lily is eight months old.
The health visitor is Claire Dunmore.
The visit is part of Lily's eight-month review.
The health visitor will assess Lily's weight, feeding, sleep, movement, and the mother's wellbeing.
The health visitor confirms that information shared during the visit will remain between her and the mother's GP unless there is a concern for someone's safety.
Lily is currently on four bottles per day.
Each bottle contains seven ounces of milk.
Lily does not finish the night bottle every night.
Lily is trying finger foods such as bits of toast and banana.
Lily gags when eating finger foods, which concerns the mother.
The health visitor explains that gagging is normal in infants and different from choking, which is silent.
Lily goes to bed around seven in the evening and wakes once around three in the morning for a bottle.
Mason wakes up earlier than Lily and is more difficult to soothe.
Dean, the father, works on lorries, Monday to Friday, and returns on weekends.
The mother is alone during the week with the children.
The mother's mother (grandmother) helps out on Tuesdays with Mason.
Mason spends 15 hours a week at Little Acorns nursery.
The mother reports financial strain, describing the household as 'tight'.
The household is currently on Universal Credit and receives money from Dean.
The household is on a key meter, which has led to a significant increase in electricity costs.
The mother reports feeling tired and bored, especially in the evenings.
The mother consumes a bottle of wine every night, most nights, when the children are in bed.
The mother confirms she drinks a bottle of wine every night, most nights, from the Co-op, starting around eight o'clock.
The mother describes the wine as a standard bottle, 75 centilitres.
The mother reports smoking a joint of cannabis a few nights a week, only when the children are in bed, and never in front of them.
The mother smokes cannabis in the garden, outside the back door, so it is not in the house.
The mother denies ever using cocaine or any other drugs.
The mother admits she has fallen asleep on the sofa and not heard Lily crying when she was awake, and that Mason has woken her multiple times.
The health visitor provides the number for the Harbridge Energy Fund, which offers top-ups for households on key meters.
